Simulate a small breeding population

Source: R/simulate.R
simulateBreeding.Rd

Generates a pedigreed population with markers and a heritable trait, for examples, tests and teaching. Founders are unrelated; later generations are produced by mating sampled parents, and each offspring inherits one allele from each parent at every marker, so the simulated genotypes and the pedigree agree with each other.

Usage

simulateBreeding(
  n_ind = 50,
  n_marker = 200,
  n_founder = 10,
  genotyped = NULL,
  n_qtl = 20,
  h2 = 0.4,
  missing = 0
)

Arguments

n_ind

Number of individuals in total.

n_marker

Number of markers.

n_founder

Number of unrelated founders. Capped at n_ind; at least two are needed if there are to be any offspring.

genotyped

Number of individuals with genotypes, taken from the most recent ones. Defaults to all of them.

n_qtl

Number of markers with an effect on the trait.

h2

Narrow-sense heritability of the simulated trait, between 0 and 1.

missing

Proportion of genotype calls set to NA, between 0 and 1.

Value

A BreedingExperiment object with a phenotype column and the true breeding value in colData.

Details

Set genotyped below n_ind to leave some individuals ungenotyped, which is the situation Hmatrix() is designed for. The genotyped individuals are the most recent ones, so the ungenotyped are the earlier generations, as in a programme that began genotyping part way through.

Note that n_founder defaults to 10 and is capped at n_ind, so a call such as simulateBreeding(n_ind = 8) returns eight unrelated founders and no pedigree structure at all. Ask for more individuals than founders to get relatives.

The trait is scaled so that the genetic variance is h2 and the residual variance is 1 - h2, and trueBV in the column data is the genetic component on that scale.

The function draws random numbers but does not set the seed itself. Call set.seed() beforehand if you need the same population twice.

See also

BreedingExperiment(), Hmatrix()

Examples

set.seed(1)
be <- simulateBreeding(n_ind = 25, n_marker = 100)
be
#> class: BreedingExperiment
#> markers: 100  individuals genotyped: 25 
#> assays(1): genotype
#> phenotypes(2): phenotype trueBV
#> sequences(5): chr1 chr2 chr3 chr4 chr5
#> pedigree: 25 individuals (25 genotyped, 0 not; 10 founders)
head(as.data.frame(colData(be)))
#>          phenotype     trueBV
#> ind001  0.03138471  0.5371443
#> ind002  1.32499010 -0.2571695
#> ind003 -0.43750356 -0.2558675
#> ind004 -0.80497722 -0.1144826
#> ind005 -1.16160565 -0.1101137
#> ind006 -0.71358531 -0.2611992

# a population where only the recent individuals were genotyped
part <- simulateBreeding(n_ind = 30, n_marker = 100, n_founder = 6,
                         genotyped = 20)
c(pedigree = nrow(pedigree(part)), genotyped = ncol(part))
#>  pedigree genotyped 
#>        30        20
